open_points.subject: A05 proof failure determinism for phases 7 and 9
open_points.text: "A proof checks one flow version in this order of phases... the first check that fails is the result" with phase 7 as "cycles: the graph of nodes and edges is acyclic" and phase 9 as "reach: at least one output of every function node reaches..."
open_points.question: When phase 7 or phase 9 fails in multiple places, which exact node/edge/output must be reported as the single "first" failure?
options: Report only a phase-level failure with no node/edge identity
Report the lexicographically first involved node/edge/output by a defined order
open_points.default_guess: Report the lexicographically smallest involved node/output to keep results deterministic.

open_points.subject: A10/A09 request_digest input for approvals
open_points.text: A10 rule 7 says approvals cover "every header the kernel sends" and multipart parts include "name, media type and the SHA-256 of its content"; A09 rule 2 defines multipart value parts as "a value part carrying its canonical JSON" but does not fix their media type or which auto-added transport headers count.
open_points.question: Exactly which headers and multipart part media types are included in request_digest, especially auto-generated headers (Host, Content-Length, User-Agent, multipart boundary)?
options: Digest only explicitly constructed headers (required headers + credential header name + explicit content headers)
Digest all on-wire headers including library-added ones
Digest explicit headers, but normalize/exclude volatile values like multipart boundary
open_points.default_guess: Include only explicitly constructed headers and exclude transport-added volatile headers from digest input.

open_points.subject: A09 path placeholder validation versus file carriage
open_points.text: Proposal-time shape check says each `{name}` path placeholder must match an input port whose schema `type` is `string` or `integer`, but it does not say the port must be `value` carriage.
open_points.question: Must a binding be refused at proposal time if a path placeholder names a `file` carriage input port?
options: Refuse at proposal time (path placeholders may reference only `value` ports)
Allow proposal and fail pre-send when runtime value cannot be placed

open_points.subject: A03 mapped-node sandbox granularity
open_points.text: A03 rule 1: "Every function execution... runs in a fresh isolated environment"; A03 rule 3: for mapped nodes, `run` is called once per element.
open_points.question: For a mapped function node, is each element call a separate sandbox execution (fresh environment each time), or are all element calls made inside one sandbox instance?
options: One sandbox per mapped node pass, multiple calls inside it
